research_contract.question: Can an Agent-invariant forecast of future task difficulty select a local historical benchmark that predicts unseen future Agent pass rates better than full history?
research_contract.mechanism: Compress each Task's reference-Agent response vector to an ordinal solve-rate state, forecast the next local state distribution without later-created cross-repository Tasks, and select a local state-matched subset.
research_contract.reason: The first-wave joint response state encoded panel identities and failed leave-one-Agent transfer. A scalar difficulty state keeps only response structure that can plausibly transfer to a new Agent.
non_solutions: searching the state count, cut points, Markov prior, local strength, horizon, or budget after outcomes open
using any held-out Agent outcome to fit, forecast, or select
using other-repository Tasks created after the target Origin cutoff
promoting a candidate from the opened development panel
adding a generalized trainer or runtime service for one experiment caller

rolling_origin.repository_scope: one repository per Origin and Selection
rolling_origin.cross_repository_cutoff: created_at no later than the final target-history Task

difficulty_representation.reference_agents: all eleven opened development Agents for the primary fit; all except the evaluated Agent for leave-one-Agent-out
difficulty_representation.task_score: number of reference Agents resolving the Task divided by the number of reference Agents
difficulty_representation.missing_result_policy: not allowed; every official result is normalized over the exact 500-Task denominator before state construction

fixed_algorithms.forecast: empirical difficulty-state distribution in the final complete five-Task history block
mean of the next five state distributions from a first-order transition model initialized at the latest local state
fixed_algorithms.training_prior: average repository-level transition matrices over cutoff-eligible non-target repositories

selection_rule.allocation: Enumerate every feasible five-state integer count vector that sums to ten and does not exceed local-history availability; minimize L1 distance between its normalized histogram and the forecast distribution, then break exact ties by the count vector.
selection_rule.within_state: take the most recent Tasks, breaking time ties by instance_id
selection_rule.future_outcome_access: Selection membership is materialized before future outcomes are read

diagnostics.primary_loss: mean across evaluated Agents of absolute selected-history versus future-block pass-rate error
diagnostics.primary_contrast: candidate loss minus full-history loss; negative favors Selection

aggregation.repositories: equal in the wide and deep views

random_calibration.sampling: independent uniform ten-Task subset at every repository-local Origin

temporal_null.rule: shuffle complete eleven-Agent response vectors within repository, refit every cutoff-aware transition model, and rematerialize every Selection

agent_transfer.rule: For each development Agent, construct states, fit, forecast, and select using only the other ten Agents, then evaluate only the omitted Agent.

required_outputs: forecast error and selected-to-forecast representation error
selection, transition, source, plan, and result digests

holdout_open_gate.priority: All requirements must hold. A boundary value fails a strict below requirement.

authority.development_result_blobs: the eight entries frozen in agent-panel-extension-plan.json
authority.holdout_result_blobs: forbidden until this plan's complete gate passes
authority.raw_result_policy: ignored local paths only; commit compact normalized evidence and digests
